mission.brief: Use the simulated find command to discover the regular file named handover.txt beneath Projects. Read that file after any changes. Discovery and reading are separate action objectives; finding other paths or reading an unrelated note does not earn them. Equivalent supported start paths and filter order count.
constraints: All paths and files are virtual. Commands act immediately; there is no Apply step and no host access.
Use only the syntax in Command reference. No quotes, wildcards, shell expansion, pipes, recursion, links, archives, or unsupported options.
Relative and absolute paths are equivalent. The final state and explicitly named activity evidence earn credit; no exact transcript is required.
File-management commands may change only descendants of /home/learner. Other paths and mutation-root nodes are pinned.
Any actual filesystem change clears cat/find verification. Read or discover the final result again. Skipped no-clobber commands do not clear evidence.

objectives.label: Action: discover the handover with supported find

hints: Listing one directory does not inspect all its descendants. Try the supported discovery command.
Start find at Projects and filter by regular-file type and exact name. The filters may be in either order.
find /home/learner/Projects -name handover.txt -type f, then cat the returned path.

/home/learner/Projects/site/docs/handove.content: Handover: keep reference copies and check final locations.

lesson.goal: Discover handover.txt beneath Projects with find, then read it.

steps.explanation: find walks the virtual tree. -type f keeps regular files; -name uses an exact basename here, with no wildcards.
Use the returned absolute path to read the file. Reading alone cannot establish the find objective.
steps.expected: Handover: keep reference copies and check final locations.
